Cieszowa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Cieszowa, Poland

Not demolished. Cieszowa was once home to one of Silesia's most populous Jewish communities in the early 18th century, though numbers declined drastically through the 19th century - just 45 residents by 1830, 18 by 1855, and none recorded after 1905. Sources disagree on this cemetery's founding: researcher Mark Brann cites evidence of a 1690 cemetery tax and a 1650-dated matzevah, while historian Marcin Wodziński argues for an 18th-century origin instead. The cemetery remained active into the early 20th century; after the last local Jews departed, oversight passed to the local Catholic parish, with a regional kehillot committee seeking restoration funding. The site survived WWII intact but fell into disrepair afterward - a 1988 survey found only 28 of 156 original tombstones still standing. A 2008 windstorm further damaged the trees and remaining stones; local community activists have since led restoration efforts.
